# Devicepool

> Devicepool is an open source, self-hosted device farm for iOS simulators and Android emulators, for your team, your CI and your AI agents.

Devicepool runs iOS simulators and Android emulators on Macs you own and lends them out one at a
time. A developer runs a React Native or Expo app on a leased device with Fast Refresh. CI runs
Maestro flows split over several fresh devices and gets one JUnit report. An AI agent such as
Claude Code, Codex or Cursor takes a device over MCP, taps through the app and reads the screen.
A person opens a device in the browser and records a bug as a link. When a lease ends,
Devicepool deletes the device and clones a fresh one. It is free under Apache-2.0, needs no
account, sends no telemetry and works offline.

What it does not do:

- It does not run iPhones. Android phones over USB are experimental and have never run on real hardware.
- It does not host anything. It needs a Mac with Xcode that someone on the team looks after.
- It has no Appium endpoint.
- It is early. It is not on npm yet, and it is installed from a clone of the repository.

Requirements: a Mac, Node 22.18 or newer, pnpm, Xcode with an iOS simulator runtime, Homebrew,
and idb (`brew tap facebook/fb && brew install idb-companion`, `pipx install fb-idb`).
`devicepool doctor` checks them. Install and start it with `git clone`, `pnpm install`,
`npm install -g ./packages/devicepool` and `devicepool up`. The README has the exact commands.
It serves plain HTTP on your network until you put TLS in front.

- [Docs index](docs/index.md): every page in one list

## Guides

- [AI agents](docs/guides/agents.md): connect Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any MCP client, the MCP tools, and the REST API
- [Your Expo or React Native app](docs/guides/expo.md): `devicepool run ios` with Fast Refresh and React Native DevTools
- [Maestro flows](docs/guides/maestro.md): `devicepool run maestro` with shards, retries and a JUnit report
- [GitHub Actions](docs/guides/github-actions.md): run Maestro flows on every pull request
- [XCUITest](docs/guides/xcuitest.md): run XCUITest on leased simulators
- [Android](docs/guides/android.md): Android emulators and Espresso
- [Recordings](docs/guides/recordings.md): record a bug as a link with video, timeline and app log
- [Device images](docs/guides/device-images.md): simulators kept ready with an app installed and a locale set
- [Embed a screen](docs/guides/embed-screen.md): a live device in a page of your own
- [Night QA](docs/guides/night-qa.md): book devices for a window and let an agent test overnight
- [More Macs](docs/guides/more-macs.md): add Macs, or run the broker in Docker or Kubernetes
- [Single sign-on](docs/guides/sso.md): OpenID Connect with groups mapped to teams and roles
- [Unattended](docs/guides/unattended.md): start Devicepool at login or at boot
- [Isolation](docs/guides/isolation.md): what a leased app can reach on the Mac

## Alternatives

- [All alternatives](docs/alternatives/index.md): open source alternatives to hosted device clouds
- [Maestro Cloud](docs/alternatives/maestro-cloud.md): run the same Maestro flows on your own Macs
- [AWS Device Farm](docs/alternatives/aws-device-farm.md): for tests that run on simulators and emulators; Device Farm has real phones
- [BrowserStack App Live](docs/alternatives/browserstack-app-live.md): test by hand in the browser on simulators and emulators; App Live has real phones
- [Appetize](docs/alternatives/appetize.md): stream simulators and emulators to the browser for your own team
- [Expo Simulators](docs/alternatives/expo-simulators.md): remote simulators for developers, CI and agents on your own Macs

## Comparison

- [How Devicepool compares](docs/comparison.md): Devicepool, Simlock, Argent, Tapflow and Expo Simulators feature by feature, and a dated table of hosted prices

## Numbers

- [Measured speed](docs/numbers.md): 52 frames a second in the browser over HTTPS or localhost (38 on a plain-HTTP LAN) and 87 ms from saving a file to the change on the device, on one Mac, with the method
